text:
maya: Heads up — observed a ~18% token throughput regression on prod qwen2.5 cluster after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Flamegraph + perf counters attached to thread.

gavin: saw it too. regression starts when sequences exceed ~384 tokens; throughput drops and latency p99 spikes. suspect kernel fallback for attention path.

leo: I reproduced locally on a subset of private GPUs. profiler shows kernel_choice switching from fast_fused_attention -> fallback_attention for head_size=128 + kv_head_dim=64 cases. odd because model spec expects kv_head_dim==head_dim/2 for this variant.

ciara: that mismatch rings a bell — we recently added permissive kernel matching for autokernel to allow kv dim mismatch across mixed checkpoints. maybe the selector now prefers a new matmul kernel that does not handle packing efficiently, causing extra memcopies.

maya: attaching short dump of selector decision for a single request (trimmed):
```
request_id=abc123
model=qwen2.5
seq_len=512
heads=64
head_dim=128
kv_head_dim=64
selector: tried=optimized_fused_gemm (rejected: alignment 128->64 mismatch)
selector: tried=custom_attention (accepted: fallback_multipass)
````

gavin: in the flamegraph the top cpu wall is copy_kv_cache + layout_transform. That explains extra mem bandwidth. Also see more small kernels getting scheduled (many launches).

leo: quick experiment — forcing kernel hint to optimized_fused_gemm returns throughput to baseline for the same tensor shapes, but correctness needs validation (we might be relying on zero-initialized KV layout differences).

ciara: two actionables: 1) hotfix: change kernel-selector to prefer fused path for qwen2.5 when head_dim % kv_head_dim == 0 and seq_len > 256, 2) longer: add a lightweight unit test that runs multiple token-lengths + multilingual tokenizer edgecases to catch layout-induced fallbacks.

maya: +1 on tests. Also we saw tokenization causing effective seq_len increases because of multi-ling CJK whitespace handling — e.g., a 300-char prompt became 420 tokens after tokenizer splits. That pushed many requests into fallback path.

gavin: logging note: add tokenized_len to perf logs for a window. helps correlate tokenizer blowups -> kernel-choice changes.

leo: filed a small PR: set kernel_selector.preference[qwen2.5]=['fused_gemm','custom_attention'] with a guard for head/kv dims. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6243 (wip).

ciara: also found an ALiBi vs RoPE mismatch in some mixed checkpoints — if the model was converted with ALiBi-but-runtime assumes RoPE-scaling, that changes kv offsets and prevents kv cache reuse (invalidations), adding mem churn. We should detect positional scheme at model load and force compatible kernel profiles.

maya: agreed. For now, rolling a canary patch to the selector on 2 hosts. infra-bot: please start canary deploy on qwen2.5 pool id qwen2-asia-04 with selector hints from leo's PR.

infra-bot: deploy requested: canary start queued -> started on qwen2-asia-04. Canary id=cny-1942. Logs will stream to #eng-runtime.

gavin: I'll run a targeted perf regression harness across languages: en, zh, ja, ko, ar with batch sizes 1/4/8 to capture tokenizer-induced length variance. If we reproduce, we can toggle the selector flag off and revert.

leo: note to self: add a small synthetic that crafts mismatched kv_head_dim to exercise fallback path — we were missing that in CI.

ciara: long-term: suggest adding a kernel compatibility matrix per model variant (head_dim, kv_dim, pos_scheme) so selector picks the cheapest kernel that preserves semantics (and we can add memcopy penalty into cost model).

maya: thanks all. I'll monitor canary and coordinate rollback if p99 > 1.5x baseline. If anyone sees correctness regressions, ping me + gavin immediately. :thumbsup:
